title: Replace from the right sequence
situation: The specification was filed new in 0000 and replaced in 0002. You are building 0005 with another revision.
question: Which leaf should the 0005 replace target?
options: The 0000 leaf, because it is the original
The 0002 leaf, the one that is current
why: A replace must point to a leaf that is current. The 0000 leaf was already replaced; targeting it again is a high-severity lifecycle error.

title: Deleting twice
situation: A superseded stability protocol was deleted in 0003. A colleague's draft for 0006 deletes it again 'to be safe'.
question: What happens to the second delete?
options: It is a lifecycle error: the target is no longer current
why: Delete, like replace, must target a current leaf. Once deleted, a leaf cannot be acted on again in v3.2.2.

title: Renamed file, broken lifecycle
situation: An updated batch analyses document arrives named batch-analyses-2026.pdf instead of batch-analyses.pdf. The publisher files it with operation new.
question: What does the reviewer now see under 3.2.P.5.4?
options: Two batch analyses documents, old and new
why: Lifecycle follows the leaf, not the file name. Filed as new, the update sits beside the old one. It should have been a replace targeting the 0000 leaf; the new file name is then fine.

title: Append or replace
situation: Twelve-month stability data must be added. The 6-month report in 0000 is still valid and the company wants reviewers to see both.
question: Which operation fits best?
options: Replace with a complete updated report
Append the 12-month update to the 0000 leaf
why: Append adds to an earlier leaf without replacing it. Many companies prefer a complete replacement report instead, which is also correct, but here the brief is to keep both visible and linked.

title: Forms in every sequence
situation: Sequence 0004 is an amendment. Form FDA 356h from 0000 is still in the current view.
question: How is the 356h for 0004 filed?
options: Not needed: the 0000 form still applies
why: The application form and the cover letter belong to each submission. They are filed new every time, so the validator does not treat them as duplicates.

title: Related sequence in the EU
situation: The MAA started with 0000. Responses to the Day 120 list of questions go in 0003; validation responses went in 0001 and 0002.
question: What is the related sequence of 0003?
options: 0000, the sequence that started the procedure
why: In the EU envelope, related sequence points to the sequence that started the procedure, so every response in the MAA names 0000.

title: Withdrawn document
situation: A nonclinical report was filed by mistake in 4.2.3.7 in 0001 and must no longer be considered.
question: How do you remove it from the current view?
options: Replace it with a blank page
Ask the agency to ignore it
why: Published sequences cannot change. A later sequence removes the leaf with a delete operation. In eCTD v4.0 the same intent is a suspended context of use.

title: Study tagging after an update
situation: In 0003 you replace the HRP-301 study report (5.3.5.1) with a corrected version.
question: What does the replacement leaf need in the US?
options: Study ID HRP-301 and a file tag, so a study tagging file in 0003 groups it
why: Study tagging files group the documents of each sequence. The new leaf needs the same study ID and its file tag, so the reviewer still sees it under HRP-301.
